A1.justification: Both complete 24-page PDFs describe the same DynFaceRestore work. The main text, Appendices A-D, equations, tables, and figures are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original restoration experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, quantitative comparisons in Tables 1-3, and additional ablations and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix analyses of guidance, kernel refinement, starting steps, and restoration models.

M1.justification: Sections 3-4 and Algorithms 1-3 retain the same Gaussian blur mapping, starting-step lookup, regional guidance adjustment, kernel refinement, and multiple-guidance procedures. No architecture, objective, or inference component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions train on FFHQ and evaluate CelebA-Test, LFW-Test, WebPhoto-Test, and Wider-Test. The appendix examples involving old photographs and global versus spatially varying degradation are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 retain the same ten comparison methods. Table 9 also retains the same GFP-GAN, RestoreFormer, and SwinIR comparisons, with identical comparator membership within each experiment.

E3.justification: The degradation pipeline, test-set sizes, metrics, FID reference datasets, and pretrained diffusion-model settings remain unchanged. The appendix ablation settings and training procedures also match.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix B retain the same component ablations, kernel-mismatch analysis, guidance-map visualization, guidance-count comparisons, starting-step tests, and restoration-model substitutions. Appendix D retains the same failure cases.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the same point estimates and plots are presented.

E6.justification: All quantitative entries and qualitative examples match, including the appendices. For example, Table 1 retains DynFaceRestore's PSNR of 24.349 and FID of 14.780; Table 2 retains FIDs of 42.515, 95.317, and 36.052.

T1.justification: Equations 1-24, the optimization definitions, diffusion formulation, and starting-step reasoning are unchanged. Minor spacing and internal hyperlink-anchor differences do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about dynamic blur mapping, diffusion timesteps, regional guidance, and balancing fidelity with perceptual quality.

C2.justification: The fidelity-quality interpretations and WebPhoto sample-size caveat remain unchanged. Appendix D retains the same limitations concerning computational cost, old-photo degradation, and spatially varying degradation.

D1.justification: V2 adds a clickable project-page pointer at the end of the abstract, absent from v1. Implementation specifications and hardware information remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the linked site's contents or code/data availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the 43 bibliography entries are unchanged. The positioning relative to GAN, codebook, and diffusion approaches remains the same.

P1.justification: V2 adds 'Project page at Link' to the abstract, changes 'Appendix B.3' to 'Sec. B.3' in Appendix A.4, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The abstract addition and Appendix A.4 wording edit produce localized text reflow. Figures 1-19 and Tables 1-9 retain their content, captions, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: V2 adds a project-page pointer and makes small presentation edits while preserving the method, experimental evidence, analyses, and limitations. The pointer provides a navigational convenience, but the PDFs establish no substantive correction or added reproducibility material that meaningfully changes overall paper quality.
